statement.text:
(P. Wesolek). The acronym tdlc stands for totally disconnected and locally
compact, and tdlcsc for tdlc and second countable. Let Res(G) denote the intersection
of all open normal subgroups of a topological group G. The class of elementary tdlcsc
groups is defined as the smallest class E of tdlcsc groups such that
  (1) E contains all second countable profinite groups and countable discrete groups;
  (2) E is closed under taking closed subgroups, Hausdorff quotients, directed unions
       of open subgroups, and group extensions.
This class admits a well-behaved, ordinal-valued decomposition rank ξ defined recur-
sively as follows: ξ({1}) = 1, and if G ∈ E is a union of an increasing sequence (Oi )
of compactly generated open subgroups, then ξ(G) = supi {ξ(Res(Oi ))} + 1.
    What is the supremum of the decomposition ranks of elementary tdlcsc groups?
In particular, is it countable?                                               C. Reid
